AttemptRow.description:
§11 risk 2: one attempt this run made, including the declared
transient-class retry. A run that executed once records one attempt, so a
retried run cannot be mistaken for a clean first-attempt run.

reason.description: Why THIS attempt happened. `initial` for the first; otherwise the declared transient class that caused the retry. The class grows only by PR with the failure named.
reason.title: Reason

AttemptRow.title: AttemptRow

description:
`dispatch_exit.v1`, at
`runs/_dispatch/{job}/{dispatch_id}.exit.json` (`crucible.keys.
dispatch_exit_key`), written by `crucible.dispatch_exit` from the box's
EXIT trap — and by the bootstrap shell when the box died before the wheel
was installed.

**Why this document exists** (`alpha-engine-config-I11050`). An absence
page could say *no manifest*; it could not say *why*, and it ended by
telling a human to go and look at a box that EC2 had already purged. The
evidence was never missing — every dispatched instance shipped a complete
CloudWatch stream — but nothing joined the three surfaces that each knew
the instance id. This is the join, written by the only party that knows
its own exit code before the process ends.

**It does not replace the manifest.** `crucible/AGENTS.md` rule 1
("manifest or it did not happen") is unchanged: a run that produced
something writes a manifest, and `manifest_written` here RECORDS whether
it did rather than standing in for it. The one path that deliberately
writes no manifest — a spot-reclaimed attempt, suppressed so two attempts
cannot both claim one key — is exactly the path this document makes
honest.

Every field is required and nullable rather than optional with a default,
the same rule `SignalsRow` states: an omitted field is indistinguishable
from a forgotten one.

argv.description: what the box was actually told to run, verbatim. Empty is legal (a handler taking no arguments); absent is not.
argv.title: Argv

attempts.description: this dispatch's attempt ladder as the box was told it (`CRUCIBLE_DISPATCH_ATTEMPTS`), or `null` on a bootstrap failure that never read it.
attempts.title: Attempts

console_tail.description: the last 4000 characters of the box console, or `null` when there was none. Bounded — see DISPATCH_EXIT_CONSOLE_TAIL_MAX.
console_tail.title: Console Tail

dispatch_id.description: the dispatch this record terminates — the same path segment `crucible.keys.dispatch_key` writes the REQUEST under, which is what joins the two documents.
dispatch_id.title: Dispatch Id

exit_code.description: the process exit status the trap observed. 143 is a signal exit (128+SIGTERM), which on this substrate is a reclaim or a shutdown.
exit_code.title: Exit Code

expected_manifest_key.description: the key this dispatch's manifest binds to, as the BOX resolved it — the authoritative answer to 'which manifest', written by the party that actually wrote (or did not write) it.
expected_manifest_key.title: Expected Manifest Key

finished_at_utc.description: RFC 3339, UTC, `Z`. When the trap ran — which is the only instant a reader can age this record against.
finished_at_utc.title: Finished At Utc

instance_id.description: the box. It is also the CloudWatch stream name, which is how a reader gets from this record to the full console without deriving anything.
instance_id.title: Instance Id

last_error_line.description: the last line of the console that names a failure, or `null` when the box exited clean. This is what an absence page renders, so a page names a cause in the words the box used rather than in the detector's.
last_error_line.title: Last Error Line

manifest_written.description: did this attempt write its manifest? `false` with `exit_class: spot_reclaimed` is the DECLARED suppression; `false` with any other class is a run that died before it could record itself.
manifest_written.title: Manifest Written

next_attempt_dispatch_id.description: the dispatch id the successor attempt will be recorded under when `redispatch_expected` is true and this attempt could name it, else `null`. A detector that has it checks one key instead of listing a prefix.
next_attempt_dispatch_id.title: Next Attempt Dispatch Id

redispatch_expected.description: did this attempt end declaring that another attempt is owed? A reclaimed attempt writes no manifest because another one will; this is that promise, recorded where a detector can check whether it was kept.
redispatch_expected.title: Redispatch Expected
